clue.text: Shares a room and has a big laugh

definitions.meaning: people who double up share sleeping quarters
to double up is to bend over in helpless mirth

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both bunking together and doubling over with laughter.

clue.text: The last letter one had from Athens

definitions.meaning: the final character of the Greek alphabet
a letter one might receive from Athens, read as a Greek character

explanation.surface: Someone receives a final piece of correspondence posted in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega closes the Greek alphabet, and a Greek alphabet character is what Athens would send.

clue.text: If successful he gets a lot knocked down

definitions.text: If successful he gets a lot knocked down

parts.words: If successful he gets a lot knocked down
parts.note: at an auction the winning offerer has the lot knocked down to him by the gavel, not beaten up

explanation.definitionFit: At auction, the person making offers wins a lot when the hammer falls in their favour.

clue.text: Book flight from Egypt

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a plane trip out of Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the biblical book and the mass departure of the Israelites from Egypt carry this name.

clue.text: Superior pep-pill?

explanation.definitionFit: Higher in position is the adjective; a stimulant pill is the slang noun.

clue.text: Don't speak now-the audience is plastered

definitions.text: Don't speak now-the audience is plastered

parts.words: Don't speak now-the audience is plastered
parts.note: a warning that eavesdroppers may be listening, with the listeners pictured as the plastered surfaces of a room rather than drunk spectators

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb warns that conversations may be overheard, the plastered partitions themselves being the listeners.

clue.text: Secondary consequence of fly-halfs fumble?

definitions.meaning: an indirect result following from something else
in rugby, a player dropping the ball forward commits a knock-on, and its result is read literally

explanation.walkthrough: A fly-half is a rugby position; a knock-on is the rugby offence of losing the ball forward.
explanation.definitionFit: An indirect knock-down result is the general idiom; in rugby union a forward fumble is a knock-on, whose outcome is its effect.

clue.text: Straining to hear-projection's falling

parts.note: the projecting lower edges of a roof are its eaves
falling means dropping

explanation.surface: Someone strains to catch a sound as a ledge collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: Eaves are the overhanging edges of a roof, and listeners once stood under them to overhear.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening secretly to others' conversation involves straining to catch their words.

clue.text: His work is full of administrative errors

definitions.text: His work is full of administrative errors

parts.words: His work is full of administrative errors
parts.note: the official who investigates complaints of maladministration spends his days on bureaucratic blunders, not making them

explanation.definitionFit: This official investigates complaints against public bodies, so mistakes by administrators fill his caseload.

clue.text: One may be in a state after he makes a pass

definitions.text: One may be in a state after he makes a pass

parts.words: One may be in a state after he makes a pass
parts.note: a subject falls into a trance once a mesmerist waves a hand, rather than being upset by an advance

explanation.definitionFit: A mesmerist's passes of the hand put a subject into a trance.

clue.text: Whisky, a production of island

parts.note: malt is a kind of whisky

explanation.surface: An island distils its own whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean nation made up of a small group of islands.

clue.text: Unstable mountains?

definitions.meaning: the North American range, the Rockies

explanation.definitionFit: Wobbly is the adjective; the Rocky Mountains of North America give the second sense.

clue.text: Members of band run into singer

indicators.note: the run letter goes into the singer's word

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Musicians from a group collide with a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpets, trombones and horns form the section of a band made from that metal.

clue.text: Anoint head of bishop with smaller quantity

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of bishop

parts.note: less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A bishop's head is anointed with a sparing amount of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate with holy oil is a form of sanctifying.

clue.text: Sensitive, like Molly Malone's cockles?

definitions.meaning: the Dublin ballad of the fishmonger Molly Malone has the refrain about cockles and mussels being still living

explanation.surface: A tender question about the shellfish in an old Irish song.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the heroine of an Irish folk song who sold shellfish, crying 'alive, alive-o'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awake to something means being sensitive to it; the song's cockles are sold still living.

clue.text: Cut off second try

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone is dropped from a team and then given another attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping wool or hair with blades removes it.

clue.text: Anti-gravity?

parts.note: going against the pull of the earth, as on a climbing slope

explanation.definitionFit: Climbing a slope means working against the earth's pull.

clue.text: Brave girl finally dropped addictive drug

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for a brave girl is lost

parts.note: a courageous woman is a heroine

explanation.surface: A courageous young woman finally gave up a narcotic habit.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate made from morphine, highly addictive.

clue.text: From Essex, I leave for life abroad

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words Essex, I leave

explanation.surface: Someone departs from an English county to live overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment means living away from one's homeland.

clue.text: Translated verses from China

indicators.note: translated suggests the word verses is rendered into a different form

explanation.surface: Poetry from China has been rendered into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Sèvres is fine French porcelain, named after the town where it is made.

clue.text: A very lucky and most competent…

parts.note: blest is a form of blessed, meaning very fortunate

explanation.surface: Someone fortunate and highly skilled, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of able, meaning most skilled.

clue.text: … pole with pointy head that's offensive

definitions.text: pole with pointy head that's offensive

parts.words: pole with pointy head that's offensive
parts.note: a shaft with a sharp tip used as an attacking weapon, not a rude person

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, an insulting person with a sharp head.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance-like weapon is a long shaft with a sharpened tip used in attack.

clue.text: Fussy scholar adds page to version of Dante

indicators.note: a version of the name Dante means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A finicky academic contributes a page to an edition of Dante.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessively concerned with minor details of learning.

clue.text: Fit in notices for changes

indicators.note: the word for fit goes in the word for notices

parts.note: ads are advertisements or notices
apt means fitting

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes adjustments into published notices.
explanation.definitionFit: Modifies or adjusts, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Alchemist has a small work team

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a team at work

explanation.surface: A mystic chemist runs a little team of workers.
explanation.definitionFit: In alchemy, an initiate who had mastered the secrets of the art was called this.

clue.text: Opera to look at briefly? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for looking briefly is dropped

parts.note: to scan is to glance over quickly

explanation.surface: A suggestion to glance at an opera, though not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about the singer Floria, set in Rome.

clue.text: Regiments' fans

explanation.walkthrough: The Buffs was the old name of the Royal East Kent Regiment in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buffs was a famous English regiment; enthusiasts are also called this.

clue.text: Bring up a chunk of wood

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up reads the words a chunk from bottom to top

parts.note: a slab is a thick chunk

explanation.surface: Someone hauls up a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A very light tropical timber used for models.

clue.text: Accepts a rally is possible from these footballers

indicators.note: is possible suggests a rearrangement of the words accepts a rally could yield something

explanation.surface: A football team concedes that a comeback may happen.
explanation.walkthrough: Crystal Palace is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A London club in English league football, so its players are footballers.

clue.text: Dreadfully sectarian sort of logic

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the word sectarian is badly mangled

explanation.surface: Bigoted reasoning is described as awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Descartes and his rationalist method of reasoning.
